summary: Rosiglitazone was pulled from the market in Armenia and five other countries starting in 2010 and carries a boxed warning in the United States due to heart harm [3][4]. Tests from a small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave the drug medium risk scores for both liver and heart harm [M]. Clinical trials involving the drug have cited concerns over its safety in heart failure, as well as general safety and toxicity issues [9][10]. Additionally, similar drugs have been pulled from the market for liver harm or carry boxed warnings in the United States for heart harm [5][6][7].
